Guides

When to start

The right window opens after four months and runs to about six. Readiness is about skills, but there is still a minimum age.

Key points

Not before 17 weeks, and not much later than six months. European gastroenterology guidance sets that lower limit and asks families not to wait beyond about 26 weeks.
Look for sitting, a steady head, and hands to mouth. Interest in food and a fading tongue-thrust reflex are part of the same picture. Age alone isn’t a signal to start, and neither are these skills before 17 weeks.
Hungarian and European advice are close, but not identical. In Hungary you’ll often hear ‘wait until six months’. The European position allows a start from 17 weeks if the baby is ready, and still wants solids under way by six months.

The window

The World Health Organization supports exclusive breastfeeding for about six months, and that’s the right default for a healthy baby born at term who is growing well. ESPGHAN’s 2017 position is slightly wider: don’t start before four months (17 weeks), and don’t wait beyond six months (26 weeks), because iron and energy needs rise and delaying allergenic foods has no benefit.

EFSA’s 2019 review found no harm for healthy term babies in Europe from starting anywhere in that window. That’s not a reason to aim for four months. It is a reason not to worry if a ready baby starts a few weeks before six months.

Signs to watch for

Look for a baby who can sit with support and hold their head steady, reaches for food and gets it into their mouth, and no longer pushes every spoonful straight back out. These skills protect the airway and make eating possible.

Waking at night, watching you eat, or chewing their fists are ordinary baby behaviours, and not good reasons to start. Nor is hoping it will help them sleep. First foods aren’t a sleep method.

What you will hear in Hungary

Hungary’s 2019 professional guideline on feeding healthy infants (identifier 001038) says solids may start from the beginning of the fifth month and should be under way by about six months. Exclusive breastfeeding to six months still fits within that, and many health visitors put it that way.

Some familiar charts still follow a slow ladder: fruit and vegetables first, then grains, then meat. The evidence on iron and allergy doesn’t support it. Start when your baby is ready, around six months, and include iron and the common allergens from the beginning.
